ledger.note: 5500 BCE: the Hemudu rice farmers settle the Ningbo plain south of Hangzhou Bay ("c. 5500 - c. 3300 BC"; the site "22 km northwest of Ningbo").
4000 BCE: the late Hemudu begins: "The culture may be divided into early and late phases, before and after 4000 BC respectively."

region.text: Hemudu, "22 km northwest of Ningbo", Yuyao "just south of the Hangzhou Bay in Jiangnan", and "the islands of Zhoushan"

ledger.note: 3300 BCE: the Hemudu ends ("c. 5500 - c. 3300 BC") and the Ningbo plain passes to the Liangzhu, which lists the Hemudu among its predecessors.

certainty.note: No border is recorded; Hangzhou Bay is the natural edge to the north.

notes: Hemudu culture, south of Hangzhou Bay; infobox 'c. 5500 - c. 3300 BC', early and late phases 'before and after 4000 BC'. Extent: the page gives 'just south of the Hangzhou Bay in Jiangnan in modern Yuyao, Zhejiang', the type site '22 km northwest of Ningbo' and sites 'on the islands of Zhoushan'; no area, no site count. A 90 km disc around Ningbo (which takes in Yuyao and most of the Zhoushan archipelago; the gazetteer has neither) is drawn, confidence 2. The page gives no predecessor or successor in the infobox; the Liangzhu page lists the Hemudu as one of its two predecessors ('Preceded by: Songze culture and Hemudu culture') and says the Miaoqian well technology was 'similar to that of the earlier Hemudu period', so the Ningbo plain passes to the Liangzhu in 3300 (confidence 2: year from both infoboxes, land the dossier's reading; the Liangzhu page says only 'Jiangsu, Shanghai & Zhejiang'). Majiabang: 'Some scholars assert that the Hemudu culture co-existed with the Majiabang culture as two separate and distinct cultures', others 'group Hemudu in with Majiabang subtraditions'; the dossiers keep them separate and the Hangzhou Bay is the border. Floods: 'Two major floods caused the nearby Yaojiang River to change its course' and salinized the soil, 'forcing settlers to leave' (undated, flood period 'from 5000 to 3900 BP' in a sea-level study); not drawn. The Kuahuqiao (earlier, same bay) has no dossier. No Cliopatria shape or area figure.
